definitions.explanation: The language spoken primarily in France and other Francophone countries.

examples.japanese: フランス{語|ご}を{習|なら}っている。
{大学|だいがく}で{第二外国語|だいにがいこくご}としてフランス{語|ご}を{選|えら}んだ。
examples.english: I chose French as my second foreign language at university.

examples.japanese: フランス{語|ご}は{発音|はつおん}が{難|むずか}しいと{言|い}われているが、{文法|ぶんぽう}は{英語|えいご}と{共通点|きょうつうてん}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: French is said to have difficult pronunciation, but its grammar has many points in common with English.

notes:
Follows the standard pattern for language names in Japanese: country/region name + {語|ご}. French is one of the most popular second foreign languages studied at Japanese universities, alongside German and Chinese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- フランス{語|ご}を{話|はな}す: to speak French
- フランス{語|ご}を{勉強|べんきょう}する: to study French
- フランス{語|ご}の{授業|じゅぎょう}: French class
- フランス{語|ご}{圏|けん}: Francophone area
- フランス{語|ご}{検定|けんてい}: French proficiency test (commonly called {仏検|ふつけん})

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {仏語|ふつご}: French language (abbreviated form, used in academic and formal contexts)
- {英語|えいご}: English language
- {独語|どくご}: German language
